title: Targeted plasma proteomics reveals organ damage signatures of AIDS-related and non-communicable chronic diseases-related deaths in HIV population
projectDescription: This project investigates the role of protein biomarkers in differentiating the underlying causes of mortality among people with HIV (PWH). With antiretroviral therapy (ART) significantly reducing deaths from opportunistic infections, noncommunicable chronic diseases (NCDs) have emerged as a leading cause of death in this population. Our study seeks to identify protein signatures that distinguish AIDS-related deaths from those due to NCDs, aiming to enhance early risk prediction and inform targeted interventions.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Plasma EDTA samples were collected at baseline enrollment and stored in -80℃ without any previous thawing. Analyses were performed by a high-throughput technique using the Organ Damage panel, which enables 92 organ damage-related biomarkers to be measured simultaneously. Each target protein was recognized by double antibodies and coupled with its specific complementary DNA barcode, which was subsequently quantified using a high-throughput microfluidic real-time PCR instrument, Biomark HD (Fluidigm, South San Francisco, CA).
dataProcessingProtocol: The Olink platform provides normalized protein expression (NPX) data where a high protein value corresponds to a high protein concentration, but not an absolute quantification. Proteins with a call rate <80% (i.e. less than 80% of the individuals had a valid measurement of that protein) were removed from further analysis. Values below the lower limit of detection (LOD) were replaced by LOD/2. Each protein was normalized by plate (by setting the mean=0 and standard deviation=1 within each plate).
